name: Render the web as a designed organizational artifact
text_content:
Type: structure

The transparency sheet's first item is "the org chart," and Part I of the record spends its length arguing that the org chart is the load-bearing misread; the artifact the record wants instead is one of its own open items, the web rendered as a designed organizational artifact rather than a chart (finding 15.2, P32, I6). This is the first thing a candidate reads, at the first interview, before any offer, and a lead candidate reading a box above their seat will arrive with exactly the playbook the lead rubric is built to refuse. What the render must show: the candidate's node, its adjacent nodes by seat, its domain lead by seat, the two leads and the center as the record describes them, parallel and neither above the other, and the record's own words for the structure. What it must refuse: a vertical line from the candidate's node to anything, a box, a title implying altitude, "reports to," and any whole-house chart that places the candidate at the bottom of something. It is re-rendered per seat, not once for the house. Until it exists, the field carries the record's words and the candidate's neighborhood drawn by hand, and the render is not a gate on the first interview. The owner sits under the record's visual design open item and the founders name it; this item does not decide that.

Filed by Session 5 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmhm4. Reasoning lives on the S5 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.
